expected_symptom: Capability absent: dxc rejects a declared-but-undefined function in a lib_6_x -spirv compile ('error: found undefined function') instead of emitting an Import linkage decoration for a later spirv-link step.
history: Import half (match.json, normal polarity): always-repro'd across v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607, 19 releases, linear scan; v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2003 answer 'SPIR-V CodeGen not available' and are invalid probes, so the effective SPIR-V floor postdates the 2020-01 report by 9 months. Export half (match-export.json, POLARITY INVERTED - repro means capability PRESENT): single clean transition, absent at v1.5.2010, present at v1.6.2104; likely commit 5ae95866e / PR #3234, which is inside v1.6.2104 and outside v1.5.2010 and is the only commit in the 268-commit window touching HLSLExportAttr in lib/SPIRV or Capability::Linkage - not built at that commit, so strong but unproven.
summary: Half implemented: the export side has emitted LinkageAttributes Export since v1.6.2104, but the import side still errors 'found undefined function' on main and on all 19 SPIR-V-capable releases; clang trunk emits both decorations. The next action is the design decision in the thread; this is a capability request, not a defect.
text_stale: The 2020 answers in the thread are now partly false: jaebaek's 'no relocatable code' (2020-01-10) and ehsannas's premise that the SPIR-V backend must first learn to generate linkage information (2020-04-22) no longer describe the export direction, which emits OpDecorate ... LinkageAttributes Export from v1.6.2104 onward. s-perron's 2024-07-26 comment is NOT stale and still describes the open design problem accurately.
